overview: This file consists of a single Department of State list-of-papers sheet for the subject “Economic Matters—Formosa, Taiwan.” Its sole entry describes a report from Japan, apparently dated March 15, 1939, stating that Hoshino, identified as president of the Cabinet Planning Board, considered Formosa’s industrial development to have reached its zenith and proposed Hainan Island as the next territory for development. The sheet is an archival index rather than the underlying report itself.

people.name: Naoki Hoshino
people.role: President of the Cabinet Planning Board, as stated on the sheet

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Economic Matters—Formosa, Taiwan
subfiles.about: An archival listing records a report that Formosa had reached the zenith of its industrial development and that Hainan Island should be developed next.
subfiles.summary: This Department of State filing sheet contains one entry for a report from Japan, apparently numbered 475 and dated March 15, 1939; the OCR’s year “1975” is incompatible with the collection period and the historical context. The entry attributes to Hoshino, identified as president of the Cabinet Planning Board, the view that Formosa’s industry had reached its developmental zenith. It further records his statement that Hainan Island should become the next territory developed. The underlying report is not included on the surviving page.

interest: Although only an index sheet survives here, its brief précis captures a revealing comparison between Japan’s established colonial development of Taiwan and its ambitions for recently occupied Hainan. It is useful evidence of how Japanese planners presented Taiwan as a mature model of imperial industrialization and contemplated transferring attention and resources to a new colonial frontier. The sheet also preserves a reference to an underlying report that researchers may be able to locate elsewhere in the State Department decimal files.
